READ IN FULL 21 September 2026, Acta Arithmetica XXX (1976) 241-252, received 24.10.1974, from the ICM scan at literature/sources/terras-1976-stopping-time-acta-arith-30-241-252.pdf, supplied by Philippe; matwbn 403s this session and the earlier record said the original had not been read. THE ATTRIBUTION CORRECTION NOW RESTS ON THIS TEXT, NOT ON LAGARIAS'S ANNOTATION. Terras's only asymptotic statement is Theorem 1.17, 'The sequence F(k) converges monotonely to 0'. Its proof writes the binomial tail (12), P[tau >= k] = sum_{a<=[k(1-gamma)]} n(a,k) 2^(-k) <= sum_{a<=[k(1-gamma)]} C(k,a) 2^(-k) -- which is exactly the sum Lagarias 1985 Theorem D bounds -- and then estimates it by the CENTRAL LIMIT THEOREM, (13)-(14), concluding lim F(k) = 0. He has the right sum and takes the limit; the entropy bound that turns it into 2^(-eta k) is the step he does not take. So 'density since 1976, exponent since 1985' is confirmed from the source, and the mechanism behind it is visible rather than inferred. NOTATION, AND IT IS OURS. Equation (8) sets gamma = ln 2 / ln 3, which is our beta. Definition 1.12 calls a sequence ADMISSIBLE when e_0 + ... + e_(i-1) > i gamma, our survivor condition. Definition 1.13 sets n(a,k) = the number of admissible sequences of length k with a zeros and names it the MODIFIED BINOMIAL COEFFICIENT -- our N_k with its weight refinement, under a name no novelty search would reach. Corollary 1.16 gives F(k) = sum_a n(a,k) 2^(-k). THEOREM 1.14 IS A PASCAL-TYPE RECURSION, FIFTY YEARS EARLY: with n(0,1) = 1 and n(1,1) = 0, c(a,k) n(a,k) + c(a-1,k) n(a-1,k) = n(a,k+1), where c(a,k) is the Boolean gate 1 iff a < k(1-gamma). Proposition 1.18 gives the normalised form in p(a,k) = n(a,k) 2^(-k). SETTLED 21 September 2026 (tests/research/juggler_sequence/test_terras_recursion.py, 46 checks): THIS IS THE SURVIVOR RECURSION. His Definition 1.12 admissibility is in integers 3^ones > 2^i, the laboratory's no-contracting-prefix condition verbatim; his gate c(a,k) = [a < k(1-gamma)] says the word is still active, so (11) is Pascal restricted to survivors, and stripping the gate returns all 2^k words. Verified exactly to k = 16: word_counts(k)[k-a] is the ACTIVE part of n(a,k), so Paper B's joint (length, weight) table is Terras's; N_k is his active row sum and M_k his terminal row sum; and sum_a n(a,k) = 2 N_(k-1), which DERIVES the Table A offset instead of fitting it, since admissible splits into active plus terminal. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DEPOSITED PAPER B: its subsection 'This recursion is not new' credits Zarubin (11 August 2019), Winkler (12 September 2017) and equation (48) of the September Hikawa, all three the one-index form N_k = 2 N_(k-1) - M_k, which follows from Theorem 1.14 by summing over a and splitting the row. The antecedent is 1976, in a paper the manuscript already carries as reference [4]. An attribution correction, not a retraction -- the subsection claims nothing as new -- but it is in a deposited text with a public DOI. ALSO IN THE TEXT. Theorem 1.2 periodicity mod 2^k and Corollary 1.4 the independence of the X_i, which is the residue-class structure Lagarias credits him with; Definition 1.5 the tau-stopping time against the chi of Definition 0.1; Proposition 1.8 tau <= chi; CONJECTURE 2.9, tau(n) = chi(n) for all n >= 2, which is the coefficient stopping time conjecture in the text -- Winkler's whole subject -- with Table C and verification for 3 <= n <= 250000; Theorem 2.6 the mini-max. TABLE A tabulates F(k) for k = 10..90 and 100..900 (2F(900) = 2.1075e-17), computed on a Burroughs B6700 at UC San Diego. CHECKED AGAINST OUR COUNTS, 21 September 2026 (tests/research/juggler_sequence/test_terras_table_a.py): it reproduces, at an OFF-BY-ONE read off the definitions rather than fitted. His Definition 0.1 and (0) make F(k) the density of chi(n) >= k, while our N_k counts chi > k, so F(k) = N_(k-1) / 2^(k-1). All seventeen usable rows agree, worst relative deviation 6.62e-4 at k = 40 against a five-figure printed table; the wrong alignment misses by at least 4.0e-2. SIX ROWS CANNOT TELL THE TWO APART -- k = 30, 60, 90, 700, 800, 900, exactly the free lengths where M_k = 0 and N_k = 2 N_(k-1), so the density is unchanged; a check sampling only those would have confirmed the wrong indexing. The k = 900 row is HELD OUT: the scan reads 2.1075e-17 where the counts give 2.1675e-17, one digit in the third place, at both alignments. Seventeen rows at six figures make a computational disagreement implausible and the likely cause is the reading of the scan; it is NOT recorded as an error in Terras and the hold-out is pinned in the test. HISTORY, from the closing paragraph: Lothar Collatz devised the problem in 1931; it then drew Kakutani and Hasse; Hasse coined the name Syracuse Problem during a visit to Syracuse. DOI 10.4064/aa-30-3-241-252, read off reference [6] of the August 2026 Winkler revision, not off doi.org (proxy-refused here). SEE ALSO terras-1978-density-addendum, a second paper this register did not know existed; no claim about what Terras proved about density should treat 1976 as all of Terras until that two-page addendum is read.
